transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

We need to check two things: whether warm air is getting in, or whether the meltwater isn't draining away. First, please run your fingers around the rubber seal on the freezer door. Is it torn, folded back, or does it feel loose and not seal tightly against the frame? Also, is there any food or packaging inside that might be stopping the door from closing fully?
yeah bottom corner of the seal is split about 5cm and the hinge side bottom bit looks flattened. no food stopping it, drawers arent overfull

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
That split seal is probably letting warm air in, which turns into the ice you're seeing. To get you the correct replacement part for your Indesit, I just need the model number from the rating sticker inside the fridge (usually on a side wall near the salad drawer). Once we have that, I can confirm exactly which seal to order.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its IB55532W, read it off the rating plate. is the seal push in or screwed? not sure yet

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
On the Indesit IB55532W, the freezer door seal is typically held in place by a retaining strip screwed into the inner door liner. However, because this specific model isn't clearly matched in our parts database to confirm the exact fixing method and part number, I cannot safely direct you to order the correct seal yourself. Given that the ice has returned so quickly after defrosting, it is best to call an engineer who can fit the correct seal and check if the drain is also blocked. In the meantime, ensure the door closes firmly by checking that nothing is obstructing it.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
